# PageParquetWriter

*Block · writers · `linecaster.blocks.writers`*

Writes the page records as Parquet, one file per task.

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Unit | page |
| Role | writer |
| Reads | - |
| Adds | - |
| Replaces | - |
| Comes after | - |
| Comes before | - |
| Used in | - |
| Source | [records.py](https://github.com/storytracer/linecaster/blob/main/src/linecaster/blocks/writers/records.py) |

The contract is that of `PageParquetWriter(output_folder='out/pages')`; the comes-after and comes-before rows are derived from every block's contract.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `output_folder` | `DataFolderLike` | required | the folder (local path, fsspec URI or `DataFolder`) the records go to. |
| `output_filename` | `str` | `'${rank}.parquet'` | the file name, datatrove's template (`${rank}`, ...). |
| `**kwargs` |  |  | datatrove's `ParquetWriter` arguments (`compression`, `batch_size`, `max_file_size`, ...; `schema` defaults to the page records' columns). |

## Behavior

The columns are fixed (`parquet_schema`): `schema`, `id`, `text`, `page` (the page record as a JSON
string) and `errors` (a JSON string, or null), so every row has the same columns. It reads no part in
particular. The files' flush is reported to the observers. Pages pass through.

    r0["page stream"] --> B
